Ministry Announces Bold Plan To Review The Review That Reviewed The Last Review

The Ministry of Transport unveiled its most ambitious accountability initiative to date on Thursday: a comprehensive, independent, forward-looking review of the review that was commissioned to review the findings of the previous review.

"We heard the public loud and clear," said a ministry spokesperson, gesturing at a flowchart with eleven boxes and no arrows. "They wanted answers. What they will receive instead is a process."

The new review will be conducted by a panel of distinguished individuals selected for their proven ability to be unavailable for comment. It will run for eighteen months, or until the news cycle moves on, whichever happens first. A preliminary interim provisional summary is expected in the spring, at which point it will be reviewed.

Asked whether any ferry would be repaired during this period, the spokesperson clarified that repairs fall outside the review's terms of reference, which are themselves under review.

Officials confirmed that the panel's budget has been fully allocated to a logo, a website, and a single laminated poster reading "Safety Is Everyone's Responsibility, Especially Yours."

Residents of Harborton expressed cautious optimism. "I have never felt so thoroughly reviewed," said a commuter who has taken the replacement bus for three weeks and now considers it a lifestyle.

The ministry stressed that no conclusions should be drawn until the review of the review has been reviewed, at which point a further review may be announced, pending review.

Satire. Any resemblance to an actual ministry is a failure of imagination on the ministry's part.
